A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same E-MAC framework and DroneBird dataset. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered material.

before.justification: v1 reports original counting results on four datasets, component and loss ablations, sensitivity experiments, and qualitative analyses.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds transfer, initialization, seed, efficiency, and supplementary component evaluations.

M1.justification: DEMO, SAM, optical-flow temporal fusion, the four-loss objective, and inference remain the same. Revised decoder attention and patch-ranking descriptions clarify operations already represented in v1 Algorithm 2 and Figure 7; they do not establish a changed implementation.

E1.justification: The four datasets and their original counting tasks remain unchanged. v2 adds a cross-category transfer scenario: training on VSCrowd and evaluating directly on DroneBird (Appendix A.1, Table 5), testing generalization to a different target category.

E2.justification: Table 10 adds a separately evaluated vanilla ViT baseline alongside the MultiMAE baseline already represented in v1's ablation results. The comparator membership in the main benchmark table and corresponding expanded appendix tables is unchanged.

E3.justification: v2 adds transfer evaluation, controlled comparisons using different pretrained weights, and FLOPs/FPS/parameter measurements on an RTX 3090. These extend the diagnostic protocols; the retained benchmark splits, stated training settings, and MAE/RMSE evaluation remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The appendix substantially extends the analyses with crowd-to-bird transfer, TCF comparisons across architectures, pretrained-weight controls, seed sensitivity, and accuracy–computation comparisons. It also revises the SAM visualization and adds component predictions. The original component, loss, mask-ratio, image-size, and density-distribution analyses remain.

E5.justification: Appendix A.8 and Table 11 newly report three random-seed runs on FDST, with averages of 1.30±0.022 MAE and 1.68±0.015 RMSE. v1 provides no corresponding run-count or dispersion report. This is limited to one dataset, and the meaning of ± is not explicitly defined.

E6.justification: The headline benchmark scores and original ablation values are unchanged, but substantial new results appear. Examples include transfer MAE/RMSE of 183.31/217.42 (Table 5), vanilla ViT results of 2.63/3.31 (Table 10), seed outcomes, and E-MAC's 811 GFLOPs, 16 FPS, and 98M parameters (Table 12). These are added evaluations, not same-setting improvements over v1.

T1.justification: The explicit warp/cross-attention composition and patch-density summation notation restate operations already described in v1's text, algorithms, and diagrams. The losses remain unchanged, and neither version contains additional theoretical propositions, proofs, or guarantees.

C1.justification: Both versions claim density-assisted masked modeling, adaptive foreground masking, temporal fusion, the DroneBird contribution, and superior counting performance across the same four benchmarks. Reordering the abstract and adding supporting experiments do not change these claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds explanations of DroneBird's small-target, sparsity, and motion challenges, and interprets poor transfer as a crowd–bird domain gap. It also attributes gains more explicitly to architecture rather than pretraining and discusses STGN's speed/parameter advantage. These qualify and extend the existing interpretations without changing the main conclusions.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-and-dataset access link, identifies Huawei Atlas 800/CANN and RTX 3090 hardware, and documents 16×16 patches and token-order restoration. These are reproducibility disclosures; the PDFs do not establish changes to the retained experiments' underlying implementation or hyperparameters.

R1.justification: The reference lists contain the same works. The positioning relative to image counting, video counting, and masked autoencoders, including the claimed novelty of density-assisted modeling and DroneBird, remains substantively unchanged.

P1.justification: Method exposition is substantially expanded in Sections 4.2–4.3 and Appendix A.2, replacing a brief appendix explanation with detailed token, masking, and decoding descriptions. The abstract is reorganized, experimental narratives are condensed, and the appendix gains thematic subsections. Author order, front matter, and acknowledgments also change.

P2.justification: v2 redraws the framework and detailed SAM diagrams, revises the SAM qualitative display, and adds target-size and component-prediction figures plus transfer, ablation, seed, and efficiency tables. Existing benchmark tables and several visualizations are retained and relocated or renumbered; those moves are not new evidence.

improvement.justification: New controls, seed reporting, and efficiency measurements make the existing performance claims easier to assess, while expanded method details and the code/data link improve reproducibility. The gains are bounded: seed testing covers only FDST, and new Appendix A.2 prose conflicts with Algorithm 1 over whether optical flow takes density maps or video frames. Overall, the added scrutiny and transparency outweigh these reporting weaknesses.
